gallery.title: File:File-Photograph of rockfall. Rockfalls occurs naturally along the West Mesa escarpment and have the potential-to destroy petroglyphs (d1e05cf9-912b-4e25-9659-deda0cfb1d6d).JPG
gallery.artist: NPS; photograph courtesy of Dale Kissner (Petroglyph National Monument).
gallery.description:
Photograph of rockfall. Rockfalls occurs naturally along the West Mesa escarpment and have the potential
to destroy petroglyphs or create safety hazards for visitors. In early 2005, a visitor mishap in the Boca Negra area of
the monument caused the large boulder shown in the photograph to tumble down onto the steps. A pickup truck

was stranded about 8 m (25 ft) up the escarpment; the boulder was dislodged when the truck was removed

gallery.title: File:2023-10-14 10-36-44 eclipse maximum annularity.jpg
gallery.description: The October 14, 2023 Annular Eclipse at maximum annularity (or very close to it). As seen from Petroglyph National Monument in New Mexico, United States.
categories: Solar eclipse of 2023 October 14 in Albuquerque, New Mexico

gallery.title: File:2023-10-14 Eclipse-end of Annularity NM 10-39-14 1.jpg
gallery.description: At the end of the full annularity on October 14, 2023, the moon starts breaking through the edge of the sun. Here it is just starting to and the edge of the sun is a broken line. As seen from Petroglyph National Monument in New Mexico, United States

gallery.title: File:2023-10-14 eclipse around annularity.jpg
gallery.description: composite photo of the October 14, 2023 Annular Eclipse showing full annularity and the sun before and after full annularity. As seen from Petroglyph National Monument in New Mexico, United States. The times of the photos are: 10:29:05, 10:31:38, 10:34:11, 10:36:44 (maximum annularity), 10:39:17, 10,41:50, and 10:44:23. The camera was in a fixed position so the images of the sun show their actual relative position to each other.

gallery.filename: Bird Motif in Boca Negra Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
gallery.title: File:Bird Motif in Boca Negra Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
gallery.description: This bird, according to archeologists, is created in the Rio Grande style, which developed around 1300 AD by ancestors of the modern Pueblo people.

gallery.filename: Old Petroglyphs in Piedras Marcadas Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
gallery.title: File:Old Petroglyphs in Piedras Marcadas Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
gallery.description: Although some images created on the volcanic rocks may seem recognizable, some archeologists are hesitant to interpret their meaning.

gallery.filename: Century-old Petroglyphs in Rinconada Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
gallery.title: File:Century-old Petroglyphs in Rinconada Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
gallery.description: Although most of the petroglyphs in Rinconada Canyon were made by Ancestral Puebloans about 400-700 years ago, there was also evidence of Spanish engagement. Here some people left their own marks about one hundred years ago.

gallery.filename: Animal Images in Rinconada Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
gallery.title: File:Animal Images in Rinconada Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
gallery.description: In the sixteenth century, both Spanish explorers and Mexicans came to the Rio Grande area and left evidence of their existence. In the late seventeenth century, parts of the West Mesa were associated with the Atrisco Land Grant which was awarded to colonists by the Spanish crown, and these colonists made their marks on the rocks.

gallery.filename: Old Petroglyphs in Rinconada Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
gallery.title: File:Old Petroglyphs in Rinconada Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
gallery.description: Although most of the images in Rinconada Canyon are believed to be about 400-700 years old, some petroglyphs could be thousands of years old. It is difficult to see all 1,200 images in the canyon.
